llama : scale moe down projection per expert token (#30861)

* llama : scale moe down projection per expert token

Replace the global amax rescaling for the MoE down projection with a per-expert-token factor computed by a POOL_1D max reduction along the intermediate dimension. Undo the scale on the output with the same exact power-of-two factor. Handle POOL_1D in the Meta split-state logic so a split along axis 0 becomes a replicated per-device partial result, enabling tensor parallelism.

Return the rescaled activation and the optional scale tensor through a small struct instead of an output pointer.

Assisted-by: pi:llama.cpp/ggml-org/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp-GGUF (Mac Studio, M2 Ultra, 192GB)

* server: coerce seed and stream from multipart form fields

Form fields arrive as strings, so -F seed=42 and -F stream=true were
rejected by the schema. seed joins the integer fields, parsed as a long
long so a full uint32 seed fits, and stream is read as a boolean when
it comes as a string.

items.name: b11780
items.body:
<details open>

server: add realtime transcription API (#30636)

* server: add realtime transcription API

* drop transcription_sessions

* proxy ws

* add docs

* server: let the API key middleware guard the websocket

httplib runs the pre-routing handler before the websocket upgrade, so
the API key middleware answers 401 at handshake like any other route.
This covers the router proxy, whose children run keyless, and accepts
the same key forms as HTTP (Bearer, raw key, X-Api-Key).

* server: keep realtime slots out of the prompt loop

A realtime slot waiting for audio is GENERATING with nothing to decode,
so it fell through the prompt loop and took slot_batched. A request on
a higher slot then failed can_batch_with on the task type and starved
for the whole session. Realtime slots have no prompt: the loop sets
them up once and always leaves them.

* server: start the realtime session once its slot is live

The audio stream was created in the prompt loop, which skips a slot
that cannot batch with the one generating, and session.created went out
before the task was posted: early appends failed and the reader quit,
leaving the socket open and the slot held until the HTTP timeout.

The slot now sets up its stream at launch and signals it with the begin
result, session.created waits for it, and a reader that stops closes
the socket so the session ends with it.

* server: name the committed item in input_audio_buffer.committed

Per the Realtime spec, item_id is the item made from the committed audio
and previous_item_id the one committed before it, null for the first.
committed now comes before the transcript that completes that item, and
both go out with the item switch under one lock, so a delta cannot land
between them.

* server: use the GA transcription session shape

T
